page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-32-standardlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine engineered for memory-intensive and data-heavy enterprise tasks. Built on the x86_64 processor architecture, it provides 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 252 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 7.88 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include graphical processing units or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Storage capabilities represent the defining feature of this configuration. The instance incorporates 7,516 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage partitioned across two local physical SSDs. This internal disk topology delivers high-throughput, low-latency block access directly on the host, avoiding the network overhead typical of decoupled persistent storage volumes. Workloads relying on rapid disk scratch space, transactional logging, or direct cache access operate directly against these NVMe drives.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the VM packages high memory density alongside large local solid-state storage. Deploying this hardware combination minimizes the need to configure multiple discrete instances or high-capacity network attached disks, consolidating high-IOPS operations into a single node. Because local SSD storage is ephemeral, architectures using this instance require robust data replication or frequent external snapshots to avoid data loss upon host termination.

The z4d-highmem-32-standardlssd instance is well matched for demanding database environments, such as relational databases, distributed NoSQL stores, in-memory caching systems, big data analytics engines, and high-throughput extract, transform, and load processing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-32-standardlssd is a storage-optimized instance tailored for applications requiring both significant memory capacity and low-latency storage access. The server features 32 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs paired with 252 GB of RAM, providing roughly 7.88 GB of memory per core. A central architectural component is its integrated local storage configuration, supplying 7,516 GB of local NVMe solid-state storage split across two local disks. With zero onboard GPUs and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the configuration focuses strictly on high-throughput compute and storage capability. The dense memory ratio combined with direct NVMe disk access yields solid cost efficiency for operations that would otherwise require multiple decoupled compute and storage services. As local NVMe drives are ephemeral, data persistence strategies are essential. This instance fits high-volume transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, in-memory caching nodes, and intensive analytical data pipelines.
